question: Normal anxiety is best described as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. a mild, short lived response to a threat that improves alertness and performance

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Normal anxiety is proportionate, time limited and actually sharpens attention and performance

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a complete loss of contact with reality: Loss of contact with reality describes psychosis, not ordinary anxiety

B — a fixed false belief held against all evidence: A fixed false belief is a delusion and belongs to psychotic illness

D — a permanent personality trait that never changes: Anxiety is a state response and is not a fixed personality trait

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Anxiety becomes a disorder only when it is excessive, persistent and interferes with daily functioning
option_1: a complete loss of contact with reality
option_2: a fixed false belief held against all evidence
option_3: a mild, short lived response to a threat that improves alertness and performance
option_4: a permanent personality trait that never changes

question: Which feature separates an anxiety disorder from ordinary anxiety?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. it is out of proportion to the threat, persists for weeks or months and causes significant distress or impairment

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The disorder is defined by excessive anxiety that is disproportionate, persistent and disabling

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — it occurs only during examinations: Anxiety limited to one situation may be normal or a specific phobia but is not the general rule

C — it is always accompanied by hallucinations: Hallucinations indicate a psychotic disorder and are not part of anxiety disorders

D — it lasts for a few seconds only: A few seconds of anxiety is a normal transient response

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Ask how much the anxiety interferes with work, sleep and relationships, because impairment is what guides treatment
option_1: it is out of proportion to the threat, persists for weeks or months and causes significant distress or impairment
option_4: it lasts for a few seconds only

question: A 36-year-old woman reports six months of excessive worry about her children and her job, with restlessness, easy fatiguability, muscle tension and broken sleep. Her thyroid profile and haemoglobin are normal. The most likely diagnosis is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. generalised anxiety disorder

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Free floating worry on most days for six months with motor tension and poor sleep is generalised anxiety disorder

🔍 Key Clues: 36-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a manic episode: Mania shows elevated mood, reduced sleep with high energy and overactivity

B — schizophrenia: Schizophrenia presents with delusions, hallucinations or disorganised speech

D — obsessive compulsive disorder: Obsessive compulsive disorder requires intrusive thoughts and rituals, neither of which is described

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Screen such a patient for depression and for alcohol or benzodiazepine use, since both commonly coexist with generalised anxiety disorder

question: A panic attack is best described as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. a sudden surge of intense fear with palpitations, choking and a fear of dying that reaches its peak within minutes

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A panic attack is abrupt, peaks within minutes and is accompanied by marked physical symptoms and a sense of impending doom

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — a gradual increase in worry over several weeks: Gradual worry over weeks describes generalised anxiety

C — repeated unwanted thoughts that the person tries to resist: Unwanted resisted thoughts are obsessions of obsessive compulsive disorder

D — a brief loss of consciousness with jerking of the limbs: Loss of consciousness with jerking suggests a seizure

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: A first panic attack is often mistaken for a heart attack, so organic causes are excluded before the diagnosis is made
option_1: a sudden surge of intense fear with palpitations, choking and a fear of dying that reaches its peak within minutes
option_2: a gradual increase in worry over several weeks
option_3: repeated unwanted thoughts that the person tries to resist
option_4: a brief loss of consciousness with jerking of the limbs

question: A 24-year-old man on the ward suddenly has palpitations, sweating, tightness in the chest and shouts that he is going to die. The nurse's first action is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. stay with him, speak in short calm sentences and coach him to slow his breathing

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A calm confident presence with simple instructions and slowed breathing shortens the attack and reduces fear

🔍 Key Clues: 24-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — put him in seclusion until the attack passes: Seclusion increases fear and is not justified for a panic attack

B — tell him firmly that he must control himself: An instruction to control himself increases the sense of failure and worsens panic

D — leave him alone in a quiet room to settle: Leaving the patient alone reinforces the fear of dying and is unsafe

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: After the attack, teach the patient that the symptoms are frightening but not dangerous, which reduces future avoidance
option_1: put him in seclusion until the attack passes
option_2: tell him firmly that he must control himself
option_3: stay with him, speak in short calm sentences and coach him to slow his breathing
option_4: leave him alone in a quiet room to settle

question: Agoraphobia is a fear of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. being in places from which escape may be difficult or help may not be available

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Agoraphobia is the fear and avoidance of situations where escape would be hard or help unavailable, such as crowds, markets and public transport

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — open heights only: Fear of heights alone is a specific phobia

C — speaking in front of a group of strangers: Fear of speaking before strangers is social anxiety disorder

D — contamination by dirt and germs: Fear of contamination belongs to obsessive compulsive disorder

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Patients with agoraphobia often become housebound, so the nurse plans graded outings rather than demanding an immediate return to normal activity
option_2: being in places from which escape may be difficult or help may not be available
option_3: speaking in front of a group of strangers

question: Excessive fear of being watched, judged or humiliated in social situations is called:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. social anxiety disorder

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Social anxiety disorder centres on the fear of negative evaluation by others during performance or social contact

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — obsessive compulsive disorder: Obsessive compulsive disorder is marked by obsessions and rituals

B — generalised anxiety disorder: Generalised anxiety is free floating worry about many areas rather than only social situations

C — separation anxiety disorder: Separation anxiety concerns being apart from an attachment figure

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Patients often use alcohol to face social situations, so substance use is screened for at the first assessment

question: A 30-year-old woman has such a fear of travelling in lifts that she has resigned from her job. Graded exposure has been planned. The principle behind this treatment is that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. the fear is reduced by learning to stay relaxed while facing the feared situation step by step

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Graded exposure pairs a relaxation response with increasingly difficult steps of the feared situation, so the fear response extinguishes

🔍 Key Clues: 30-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the fear can be removed by explaining that lifts are safe: Simple reassurance does not alter a conditioned fear response

B — drugs alone can abolish a specific phobia: Drugs help the accompanying anxiety but do not by themselves abolish a specific phobia

D — the patient should confront the most feared situation at once: Immediate confrontation of the worst situation is flooding, which is badly tolerated and is not the first step

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Each step must be repeated until the patient is comfortable before moving to the next one
option_1: the fear can be removed by explaining that lifts are safe
option_2: drugs alone can abolish a specific phobia
option_3: the fear is reduced by learning to stay relaxed while facing the feared situation step by step
option_4: the patient should confront the most feared situation at once

question: The three main groups of symptoms in post-traumatic stress disorder are:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. re-experiencing, avoidance and increased arousal

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The disorder combines intrusive re-experiencing of the event, avoidance of reminders and a state of heightened arousal

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — obsessions, compulsions and tics: Obsessions and compulsions belong to obsessive compulsive disorder

C — delusions, hallucinations and disorganised speech: Delusions and hallucinations indicate a psychotic disorder

D — elation, overactivity and reduced need for sleep: Elation with reduced sleep suggests mania

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Symptoms usually begin within six months of the event, and nightmares and flashbacks are the features that bring the patient to hospital
option_4: elation, overactivity and reduced need for sleep

question: A 29-year-old bus driver who was in a serious accident wakes at night drenched in sweat, re-lives the crash and refuses to travel by bus. During a flashback the nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. stay with him, call him by name, orient him to the present and keep the environment calm and safe

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Grounding the patient in the here and now with a calm presence helps terminate the flashback and restores a sense of safety

🔍 Key Clues: 29-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — switch off the lights and leave the room: Leaving him alone in the dark intensifies fear and disorientation

B — restrain him until the flashback ends: Restraint during a flashback is frightening and unnecessary

D — ask him to describe the accident in full detail: Forcing detailed recall during a flashback re-traumatises the patient

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Formal trauma-focused therapy is offered only when the patient is stable enough to tolerate it
option_1: switch off the lights and leave the room
option_3: stay with him, call him by name, orient him to the present and keep the environment calm and safe
option_4: ask him to describe the accident in full detail

question: An obsession is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. a recurrent unwanted thought that the person recognises as his own and tries to resist

🧠 Clinical Rationale: An obsession is an intrusive, repetitive and distressing thought or image that is experienced as one's own and is resisted

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — a repetitive act performed to reduce anxiety: A repetitive act performed to relieve anxiety is a compulsion

C — a belief that others are plotting against the person: Belief that others are plotting is a persecutory delusion

D — a false perception in the absence of any external stimulus: A false perception without a stimulus is a hallucination

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Because the patient recognises the thought as senseless, the distress is often hidden out of shame, so the nurse asks gently and without judgement
option_1: a recurrent unwanted thought that the person recognises as his own and tries to resist
option_2: a repetitive act performed to reduce anxiety
option_3: a belief that others are plotting against the person
option_4: a false perception in the absence of any external stimulus

question: A compulsion is best defined as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. a repetitive behaviour or mental act that the person feels driven to perform to reduce the distress of an obsession

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The compulsion is a ritual performed to neutralise the anxiety produced by an obsession, and it is not experienced as pleasurable

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — an inability to experience pleasure: Inability to feel pleasure is anhedonia, a feature of depression

C — a sudden surge of fear lasting a few minutes: A brief surge of fear is a panic attack

D — the belief that one's thoughts can be heard by others: The belief that thoughts can be heard by others is thought broadcasting

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: The ritual brings only temporary relief, and the relief itself keeps the cycle going
option_2: a repetitive behaviour or mental act that the person feels driven to perform to reduce the distress of an obsession
option_3: a sudden surge of fear lasting a few minutes
option_4: the belief that one's thoughts can be heard by others

question: A 27-year-old man washes his hands for more than an hour at a time and his hands are red and cracked. At the beginning of care the nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. set a mutually agreed time limit for washing and provide emollient for the damaged skin

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A negotiated limit that is gradually reduced protects the skin while the anxiety is contained, and skin care treats the damage already done

🔍 Key Clues: 27-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — tell him that the behaviour is silly: Calling the behaviour silly shames the patient and increases concealment

B — agree that his hands really are contaminated: Agreeing with the belief strengthens the obsession

D — stop him each time and lock the washroom: Locking the washroom and forcibly stopping him raises anxiety sharply and damages trust

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: The compulsion reduces anxiety, so the reduction must be gradual and matched to the patient's tolerance
option_1: tell him that the behaviour is silly
option_2: agree that his hands really are contaminated
option_3: set a mutually agreed time limit for washing and provide emollient for the damaged skin
option_4: stop him each time and lock the washroom

question: The treatment of choice for obsessive compulsive disorder is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor with exposure and response prevention

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A serotonin reuptake inhibitor in a higher dose combined with exposure and response prevention is the standard treatment

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — long term admission with complete avoidance of the feared objects: Avoidance maintains the disorder instead of treating it

C — a benzodiazepine alone: Benzodiazepines relieve anxiety briefly but do not treat the disorder and carry a risk of dependence

D — electroconvulsive therapy: Electroconvulsive therapy is reserved for severe depression and catatonia rather than obsessive compulsive disorder

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: The response to medication is slow, often taking eight to twelve weeks, so the patient must be warned not to stop early
option_1: long term admission with complete avoidance of the feared objects
option_2: a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor with exposure and response prevention

question: A 44-year-old man who has drunk heavily for ten years is admitted and has had no alcohol for eight hours. He is tremulous, sweating and anxious with a pulse of 110 per minute. These features indicate:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. the onset of alcohol withdrawal

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Signs of autonomic overactivity begin six to twenty-four hours after the last drink and mark withdrawal

🔍 Key Clues: 44-year-old | 110 per minute

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — an overdose of alcohol: Overdose of alcohol causes depression of consciousness and respiration, not tremor and tachycardia

B — a schizophrenic relapse: A schizophrenic relapse brings delusions, hallucinations or disorganised speech

D — Wernicke encephalopathy: Wernicke encephalopathy presents with confusion, ataxia and eye movement palsies

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Withdrawal is monitored with a scoring chart so that treatment is given before complications such as seizures develop

question: A 50-year-old man who stopped drinking three days ago is now confused, tremulous and sweating, with a pulse of 130 per minute and a temperature of 38.2 degrees Celsius. He says he can see insects on the wall. The correct interpretation is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. delirium tremens

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Confusion with hallucinations, marked autonomic overactivity and fever after abrupt withdrawal is delirium tremens, a medical emergency

🔍 Key Clues: 50-year-old | 130 per minute | 38.2 degrees Celsius

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — acute alcohol intoxication: Intoxication depresses rather than excites the nervous system

B — a simple anxiety attack: An anxiety attack causes no disorientation or visual hallucinations

D — hepatic encephalopathy: Hepatic encephalopathy also causes confusion but is accompanied by liver failure signs such as jaundice, ascites and fetor

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Delirium tremens carries a high mortality if untreated, so the patient needs a quiet well lit room, close observation and prescribed sedation

question: Which drug group is used to treat alcohol withdrawal and to prevent withdrawal seizures?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. benzodiazepines such as chlordiazepoxide

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A long acting benzodiazepine such as chlordiazepoxide controls withdrawal symptoms and reduces the risk of seizures

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — antipsychotics such as haloperidol alone: An antipsychotic may be added for hallucinations but does not prevent seizures and can lower the seizure threshold

C — selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors: Serotonin reuptake inhibitors treat depression and take weeks to act, so they do not cover acute withdrawal

D — opioid antagonists such as naltrexone: Naltrexone reduces craving and relapse over the longer term, not acute withdrawal

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Thiamine is given along with the sedative because a glucose load without thiamine can precipitate Wernicke encephalopathy

question: A patient in alcohol withdrawal develops confusion, unsteadiness of gait and paralysis of eye movements. The likely diagnosis is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Wernicke encephalopathy due to thiamine deficiency

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The triad of confusion, ataxia and ophthalmoplegia indicates Wernicke encephalopathy from thiamine deficiency

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a panic attack: A panic attack does not cause ataxia or eye movement palsy

C — alcohol intoxication: Intoxication causes drowsiness and slurred speech rather than this triad

D — an extrapyramidal reaction: An extrapyramidal reaction causes rigidity, tremor and abnormal postures

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Thiamine must be given before or with glucose, because a carbohydrate load alone can worsen the deficiency

question: A 26-year-old man dependent on heroin has not used the drug for 24 hours. He has dilated pupils, tears, a running nose, yawning, goose flesh and abdominal cramps. The most appropriate nursing action is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. provide a quiet room, fluids, comfort measures and close observation because opioid withdrawal is distressing but rarely life threatening

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Opioid withdrawal is intensely uncomfortable but seldom dangerous, so supportive care with observation is the main treatment

🔍 Key Clues: 26-year-old | 24 hours

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — restrain him to prevent injury: Restraint is unnecessary and increases distress

C — start immediate intravenous fluids and oxygen: Routine oxygen and intravenous fluids are not required in an uncomplicated withdrawal

D — give naloxone at once: Naloxone is an antagonist used for opioid overdose, and giving it would worsen withdrawal

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Record the vital signs and the withdrawal score, as the score guides substitution treatment and confirms the diagnosis
option_2: provide a quiet room, fluids, comfort measures and close observation because opioid withdrawal is distressing but rarely life threatening

question: A patient is brought in with pinpoint pupils, a respiratory rate of six per minute and deep unconsciousness after injecting a drug. The immediate antidote is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. naloxone

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Naloxone reverses opioid induced respiratory depression and stupor within minutes

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — flumazenil: Flumazenil reverses benzodiazepines, which cause sedation but not pinpoint pupils

C — thiamine: Thiamine is given to prevent Wernicke encephalopathy in alcohol dependence

D — atropine: Atropine is an antimuscarinic drug used for bradycardia and poisoning by organophosphates

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Naloxone has a shorter action than many opioids, so the patient must be observed closely for recurrence of respiratory depression

question: A 38-year-old woman who has taken diazepam for two years is admitted and her tablets are stopped abruptly by mistake. Twelve hours later she has tremor, sweating and anxiety. The most important concern is that she may develop:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. a seizure

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Abrupt withdrawal of a benzodiazepine can cause seizures and even status epilepticus because the drug has been suppressing central nervous activity

🔍 Key Clues: 38-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — tardive dyskinesia: Tardive dyskinesia follows long term antipsychotic treatment

C — neuroleptic malignant syndrome: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is a reaction to antipsychotic drugs

D — a manic episode: Mania is not a recognised withdrawal effect

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Benzodiazepines must always be reduced gradually, with the dose confirmed on admission so that the taper continues without a gap

question: A 21-year-old student who smokes cannabis daily is brought in with suspiciousness and the belief that classmates are watching him. On examination his eyes are red and his heart rate is 100 per minute. The most likely explanation is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. cannabis induced psychosis

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Heavy cannabis use, especially of high potency preparations, can produce suspiciousness and paranoid beliefs along with conjunctival injection and tachycardia

🔍 Key Clues: 21-year-old | 100 per minute

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — hypothyroidism: Hypothyroidism slows the pulse and causes lethargy and low mood

C — a manic episode: Mania shows elevated mood, grandiosity and greatly reduced sleep, none of which is described

D — obsessive compulsive disorder: Obsessive compulsive disorder does not produce persecutory beliefs

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Cannabis use worsens the course of schizophrenia, so its use is recorded in every young patient with psychosis

question: Electroconvulsive therapy is most clearly indicated in a patient who has:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. severe depression with refusal of food and a high suicide risk, or catatonia

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Electroconvulsive therapy is used when a severe mood disorder or catatonia is life threatening or has failed to respond to drugs

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — a mild specific phobia: A specific phobia responds to graded exposure

C — a personality disorder with manipulative behaviour: Manipulative behaviour is not an indication

D — obsessive compulsive disorder with mild symptoms: Mild obsessive compulsive disorder is treated with drugs and response prevention

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Consent, or the legally approved process when capacity is lacking, must be documented before the first treatment
option_1: severe depression with refusal of food and a high suicide risk, or catatonia

question: A 62-year-old man is to have his first electroconvulsive therapy in the morning. Which nursing preparation is correct?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. ensure a written informed consent, keep him fasting from midnight and ask him to empty his bladder and remove dentures and jewellery

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Consent, an empty stomach and removal of dentures, prostheses and jewellery are the standard preparations

🔍 Key Clues: 62-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — give a heavy meal at midnight to give energy: A heavy meal increases the risk of aspiration during anaesthesia

C — allow him to keep his dentures and spectacles on: Dentures and loose items can obstruct the airway or be broken during the seizure

D — withhold all regular drugs including antihypertensives for a week: Regular drugs are reviewed by the anaesthetist rather than stopped for a week

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Loose teeth and any artificial device must be recorded and removed, because the bite is strong during the fit
option_1: ensure a written informed consent, keep him fasting from midnight and ask him to empty his bladder and remove dentures and jewellery
option_2: give a heavy meal at midnight to give energy
option_3: allow him to keep his dentures and spectacles on
option_4: withhold all regular drugs including antihypertensives for a week

question: Immediately after electroconvulsive therapy, the patient should be nursed:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. in the lateral position with the airway maintained, and usually turned on to the side until conscious

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A lateral position maintains the airway and allows secretions to drain while the patient is unconscious

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — sitting upright to prevent vomiting: Sitting upright is unsafe while the patient is still sedated

B — flat on the back with the head raised and the legs lowered: A flat or head up position increases the risk of aspiration

C — prone with a pillow over the face: The prone position with a pillow over the face obstructs breathing and is never used

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Monitor the pulse, respiration and blood pressure every fifteen minutes until the patient is fully awake
option_2: flat on the back with the head raised and the legs lowered
option_3: prone with a pillow over the face
option_4: in the lateral position with the airway maintained, and usually turned on to the side until conscious

question: A patient who has had six sessions of electroconvulsive therapy complains of forgetting the names of his neighbours and the events of the last two weeks. The nurse should explain that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. the memory loss is mostly of recent events around the treatment and usually improves over weeks to months

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Post-treatment memory disturbance mainly affects the period around the course of treatment and generally improves over weeks to months

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — memory returns within a few minutes: Recovery is gradual and not a matter of minutes

C — memory loss is permanent and he must accept it: Most patients recover substantially, so it is wrong to say the loss is permanent

D — the memory loss proves that the treatment has damaged the brain: There is no evidence of structural brain damage of this kind

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Recording the patient's own account of memory problems helps the psychiatrist adjust the frequency and laterality of treatment
option_1: the memory loss is mostly of recent events around the treatment and usually improves over weeks to months
option_3: memory loss is permanent and he must accept it
option_4: the memory loss proves that the treatment has damaged the brain

question: A 33-year-old man says he does not think his drinking is a problem but attends hospital only because his wife threatened to leave. Which nursing approach is most likely to help him engage with treatment?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. use motivational interviewing to explore his own reasons for change without judgement

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Motivational interviewing accepts the patient's position, examines the advantages and disadvantages of drinking and strengthens his own motivation

🔍 Key Clues: 33-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — refuse to discuss the drinking until he admits he is dependent: Refusing to discuss the problem ends the therapeutic contact

B — warn him that he will die soon: Instilling fear does not build motivation and damages the relationship

D — confront him firmly about the harm he is causing: Direct confrontation commonly increases resistance and drop out

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Progress is measured in small steps such as attending a follow-up visit rather than in an immediate promise of abstinence
option_1: refuse to discuss the drinking until he admits he is dependent
option_2: warn him that he will die soon
option_3: use motivational interviewing to explore his own reasons for change without judgement
option_4: confront him firmly about the harm he is causing

question: A 22-year-old woman with severe anxiety is breathing very rapidly and complains of tingling in her hands and around her mouth. Which action will relieve her symptoms?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. coach her to slow and deepen her breathing, and calm her

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Tingling results from hyperventilation washing out carbon dioxide, and slowing the breathing corrects it

🔍 Key Clues: 22-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give her oxygen through a mask: Supplementary oxygen does not correct the low carbon dioxide that causes the tingling

B — sedate her at once: Sedation is used only when the anxiety cannot be settled by simpler measures

D — give her a paper bag to breathe into for half an hour: Prolonged rebreathing from a bag risks hypoxia and is no longer recommended

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Repeated episodes of overbreathing without cause should prompt a search for a physical illness such as an anxiety state complicating asthma
option_3: coach her to slow and deepen her breathing, and calm her
option_4: give her a paper bag to breathe into for half an hour

question: A 40-year-old man is admitted for the third time for alcohol dependence. On the second day the nurse finds that a visitor has brought him a bottle of country liquor hidden in a bag. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. take the bottle, record the incident and inform the treating team, and explain the ward rules to the patient and the visitor

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Removing the substance, documenting the incident, informing the team and teaching both patient and visitor follow the ward policy and protect the treatment plan

🔍 Key Clues: 40-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — allow him to drink it now and monitor him: Allowing the drink contradicts the agreed plan and can produce dangerous interactions with sedative drugs

B — return the bottle to the visitor and say nothing more: Quietly returning the bottle conceals the breach and leaves the patient exposed to relapse

C — keep the bottle in the patient's locker under supervision: Storing alcohol in the patient's locker defeats the whole purpose of admission

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Visitors must be educated on the ward rules, since well meaning relatives are a common source of contraband
option_1: allow him to drink it now and monitor him
option_2: return the bottle to the visitor and say nothing more
option_3: keep the bottle in the patient's locker under supervision
option_4: take the bottle, record the incident and inform the treating team, and explain the ward rules to the patient and the visitor

question: Choosing the correct answer from a list given in a question paper mainly tests:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. recognition memory

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Recognition is the identification of material that is presented again, as in a multiple choice question

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — procedural memory: Procedural memory is the memory of skills such as cycling

B — implicit memory: Implicit memory is shown in performance without conscious awareness

D — recall memory: Recall is the reproduction of material from memory without any cue

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Recognition is easier than free recall, which is why patients with early memory loss can still complete short answer forms accurately

question: A 10-year-old child has a mental age of 12 years. Using the ratio method, the intelligence quotient is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 120

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The quotient is the mental age divided by the chronological age and multiplied by one hundred, so 12 divided by 10 gives 1.2, which is 120

🔍 Key Clues: 10-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 12: 12 is the mental age and not the quotient

B — 100: 100 is the value when mental age equals chronological age

D — 83: 83 is obtained by dividing ten by twelve

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: A quotient of about 120 falls in the above average range, which has implications for the schooling the child needs

question: A patient who receives a token for every ward task completed and exchanges the tokens for a magazine is being influenced by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. operant conditioning with a token economy

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The ward programme shapes behaviour by reinforcing desired acts with tokens that have a later reward value

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — insight learning: Insight learning involves sudden understanding of a problem

B — observational learning: Observational learning occurs by watching and imitating another person

C — classical conditioning: Classical conditioning pairs a neutral stimulus with a reflex response and does not require a reward

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: The token economy works best with clear rules, immediate reinforcement and a written plan agreed by the whole team

question: In Maslow's hierarchy of needs, which need must be met first?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. physiological needs such as air, food and shelter

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Physiological needs form the base of the hierarchy and must be satisfied before higher needs can motivate behaviour

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — belongingness needs: Belongingness and love come after safety needs and cannot be met while basic needs are unmet

C — esteem needs: Esteem needs lie above belongingness

D — self-actualisation: Self-actualisation is the highest need at the top of the pyramid

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: A patient who is hungry, in pain or sleep deprived cannot engage with counselling, so basic needs are always attended to first
option_2: physiological needs such as air, food and shelter

question: The trait approach to personality holds that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. personality consists of stable, enduring characteristics that describe and differentiate one person from another

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Trait theorists describe personality in terms of consistent dispositions such as extraversion and conscientiousness

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — personality changes with every situation without any consistency: If behaviour were purely situation bound there would be no consistency to describe

C — personality is entirely determined by early childhood events: The psychodynamic view emphasises early childhood, whereas the trait view emphasises enduring patterns

D — personality cannot be assessed at all: Trait questionnaires are widely used and do provide a measure

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: A knowledge of a patient's usual personality helps the nurse recognise what is new or out of character and therefore clinically important
option_1: personality changes with every situation without any consistency
option_2: personality consists of stable, enduring characteristics that describe and differentiate one person from another
option_3: personality is entirely determined by early childhood events

question: A man in a dark corridor mistakes a hanging coat for a person waiting to attack him. This experience is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. an illusion

🧠 Clinical Rationale: An illusion is a misinterpretation of a real external stimulus, here the coat

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a delusion: A delusion is a fixed false belief rather than a sensory experience

B — a hallucination: A hallucination occurs without any external stimulus

C — a compulsion: A compulsion is a repetitive act performed to relieve anxiety

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Illusions are common in dim light, fever and sleep deprivation and usually disappear once the environment or the physical state improves

question: The Rorschach ink blot test is an example of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. a projective test of personality

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Projective tests present an ambiguous stimulus and are interpreted to reveal the person's inner feelings and conflicts

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — an aptitude test: Aptitude tests predict the ability to learn a specific skill

C — an intelligence test: Intelligence tests measure mental ability against a standard sample

D — an achievement test: Achievement tests measure what has been learnt

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Projective tests must be applied and interpreted by a trained psychologist, and the nurse only facilitates the appointment

question: A 45-year-old woman is told that her biopsy report is awaited. She has palpitations, a dry mouth and difficulty concentrating. According to Selye's general adaptation syndrome she is in the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. alarm stage

🧠 Clinical Rationale: In the alarm stage the body recognises the stressor and mounts the sympathetic fight or flight response

🔍 Key Clues: 45-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — recovery stage: Recovery is not a stage of the general adaptation syndrome

B — resistance stage: In resistance the body adapts and the outward signs settle while resources are consumed

C — exhaustion stage: Exhaustion occurs when adaptation fails, with collapse and illness

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Prolonged anxiety while awaiting investigations is relieved by honest information and by offering a definite time for the report

question: The ethical principle of veracity requires the nurse to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. tell the truth and not deceive the patient

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Veracity is truthfulness, and it obliges the nurse to give honest information and avoid deception

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — keep all patient information secret: Keeping information secret describes confidentiality

C — treat every patient exactly alike: Treating everyone alike describes justice

D — do the greatest good for the greatest number: Acting for the greatest number describes utilitarianism rather than veracity

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: Truthfulness must be practised with sensitivity, and hope can be offered honestly without giving false assurance
option_2: tell the truth and not deceive the patient
option_4: do the greatest good for the greatest number

question: A 31-year-old patient tells the nurse that when he is discharged he intends to kill a named neighbour. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. inform the treating psychiatrist so that the risk can be assessed and the necessary steps taken to protect the identified person

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A serious threat of harm to an identifiable person overrides confidentiality, and the treating team must act to protect that person

🔍 Key Clues: 31-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — tell the patient that he must report the threat himself: Leaving the responsibility with the patient delays protection and is not the nurse's role

C — wait for the patient to bring it up again at the next review: Delay leaves the threatened person at risk of serious harm

D — promise to keep the information entirely secret as requested: An absolute promise of secrecy cannot be given when there is a real risk to another person

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: Record the exact words used by the patient, as the assessment and any steps taken must be documented
option_1: tell the patient that he must report the threat himself
option_2: inform the treating psychiatrist so that the risk can be assessed and the necessary steps taken to protect the identified person
option_3: wait for the patient to bring it up again at the next review
option_4: promise to keep the information entirely secret as requested

question: A 48-year-old patient with capacity refuses an antidepressant that the team believes he needs. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. accept that a competent patient may refuse treatment after he has been given full information, and document the refusal and the counselling given

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Respect for autonomy means a competent informed patient may refuse treatment, and the refusal must be properly recorded

🔍 Key Clues: 48-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — ask the relatives to sign the consent form themselves: Relatives cannot consent on behalf of a competent adult

B — mix the drug into his food without telling him: Concealing a drug in food is assault and a serious breach of trust

D — discharge the patient immediately: Discharge is a clinical decision and is not a punishment for refusal

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: Refusal must be followed up with continued explanation, because many patients change their mind once their fears are addressed
option_1: ask the relatives to sign the consent form themselves
option_2: mix the drug into his food without telling him
option_3: accept that a competent patient may refuse treatment after he has been given full information, and document the refusal and the counselling given

question: Which statement about the use of restraint in psychiatric care is correct?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. it is used only as a last resort, for the shortest possible time, with a written order and continuous observation

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Restraint is used only when less restrictive measures have failed, for the shortest necessary period, under written order and continued observation

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — it may be continued indefinitely once the patient is quiet: Restraint is released as soon as the risk has fallen

B — it may be used as a punishment for misbehaviour: Restraint is never a punishment and doing so is professional misconduct

C — it may be applied by the nurse without any medical order: A medical order is required except in an emergency, and even then it must be reviewed at once

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: The need for restraint must be reviewed frequently, and the patient is checked for circulation, breathing and skin integrity throughout
option_1: it may be continued indefinitely once the patient is quiet
option_2: it may be used as a punishment for misbehaviour
option_3: it may be applied by the nurse without any medical order
option_4: it is used only as a last resort, for the shortest possible time, with a written order and continuous observation

question: For a competent adult about to receive electroconvulsive therapy, valid consent means that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. the patient has been given full information about the treatment and its risks and agrees freely in writing

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Valid consent requires full disclosure, understanding, capacity and a free decision, recorded in writing

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the relatives have signed the form on the patient's behalf: Relatives cannot give consent for a competent adult

C — the psychiatrist has recorded in the notes that the treatment is necessary: A note of medical necessity does not by itself constitute consent

D — the nurse has explained the treatment to the family: Informing the family does not replace consent from the patient

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: When the patient lacks capacity, the procedure laid down in the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 must be followed and documented
option_1: the relatives have signed the form on the patient's behalf
option_2: the patient has been given full information about the treatment and its risks and agrees freely in writing
option_3: the psychiatrist has recorded in the notes that the treatment is necessary
option_4: the nurse has explained the treatment to the family

question: A person admitted to a mental health establishment is entitled to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. information about the admission, humane living conditions and access to his nominated representative

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The law guarantees information about admission, safe and decent living conditions, and the right to communicate with and be visited by a nominated representative

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — treatment free of charge in every establishment in the country: Free treatment is provided in government establishments rather than universally

C — unconditional access to all his own sharp objects and medicines: Sharp objects and unauthorised medicines are withheld as part of safe care

D — complete freedom to leave the ward at any time without any process: Leave is governed by the admission process and by clinical risk

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nominated representative must be informed of the admission without delay and the fact recorded
option_1: information about the admission, humane living conditions and access to his nominated representative
option_2: treatment free of charge in every establishment in the country

option_4: complete freedom to leave the ward at any time without any process

question: A 25-year-old patient recovering from depression asks the 27-year-old nurse to meet him outside the hospital as a friend. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. politely decline and explain that their relationship must remain professional while he is under her care, and report the request to the nurse in charge

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Maintaining a professional boundary protects the patient from exploitation and keeps the therapeutic relationship safe and effective

🔍 Key Clues: 25-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — give the patient her mobile number so that he can contact her in a crisis: Personal contact details breach the professional boundary even with good intent

C — accept the invitation because it may improve the patient's mood: A social relationship with a current patient is a boundary violation

D — ignore the request and avoid the patient completely: Withdrawing care altogether is a form of rejection and is unethical

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: Boundary requests are common in long admissions and should be dealt with openly, kindly and without shaming the patient
option_1: politely decline and explain that their relationship must remain professional while he is under her care, and report the request to the nurse in charge
option_2: give the patient her mobile number so that he can contact her in a crisis

question: Which is the correct order for removing personal protective equipment?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. gloves, goggles, gown, mask

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Contaminated gloves come off first, then eye protection, then the gown and the mask last, with hand hygiene after each step

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — goggles, mask, gown, gloves: Gloves are the most contaminated item and must be removed before the others

C — mask, gloves, gown, goggles: The mask is the last item to be removed, not the first

D — gown, mask, goggles, gloves: This is close to the order for donning rather than for removing

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: Hand hygiene after removal is the single most important step in preventing transmission of infection

question: Which statement about oxygen administration through a nasal cannula is correct?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. oxygen should be humidified when the flow rate is above four litres per minute

🧠 Clinical Rationale: At higher flow rates the drying effect on the nasal mucosa is significant, so humidification is added

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — oxygen flow may be increased freely to 15 litres per minute through a cannula: Flows above about six litres per minute through a cannula cause severe nasal irritation and add little oxygen

C — the cannula delivers an exact inspired concentration of oxygen: A cannula gives only an approximate inspired concentration that varies with the patient's breathing

D — a nasogastric tube is required before oxygen can be given: A nasogastric tube has no relation to oxygen therapy

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: Nose bleeding and dryness are common with unhumidified oxygen, so the mucosa is inspected each shift
option_1: oxygen should be humidified when the flow rate is above four litres per minute
option_2: oxygen flow may be increased freely to 15 litres per minute through a cannula
option_3: the cannula delivers an exact inspired concentration of oxygen
option_4: a nasogastric tube is required before oxygen can be given

question: A 58-year-old man must give a sputum specimen for acid-fast bacilli. Which instruction should the nurse give?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. rinse the mouth with water and cough deeply to bring up sputum from the chest, preferably early in the morning

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Deep coughing after rinsing the mouth gives sputum from the lower respiratory tract, and morning specimens are richest in organisms

🔍 Key Clues: 58-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — collect the specimen after taking an antibiotic for two days: Antibiotics given before collection reduce the yield of organisms

B — collect the specimen after a meal: A specimen after a meal is likely to be mixed with food particles

D — spit out the saliva into the container: Saliva does not contain the bacilli and gives a false negative result

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: The container must be wide mouthed, leak proof and sent to the laboratory without delay
option_1: collect the specimen after taking an antibiotic for two days
option_3: rinse the mouth with water and cough deeply to bring up sputum from the chest, preferably early in the morning
option_4: spit out the saliva into the container

question: Which finding suggests that a patient is dehydrated?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. a dry tongue, reduced skin turgor and a low urine output with concentrated urine

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Loss of body water gives a dry tongue, poor skin turgor and a small volume of concentrated urine

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a raised jugular venous pressure: A raised jugular venous pressure indicates excess circulating volume

B — crackles at the lung bases: Basal crackles suggest pulmonary oedema from fluid overload

C — pitting oedema of the ankles: Pitting oedema indicates fluid overload rather than dehydration

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Pearl: A useful bedside check is the hourly urine output, which should be at least half a millilitre per kilogram per hour
option_4: a dry tongue, reduced skin turgor and a low urine output with concentrated urine

question: Oxygen is given to a patient with an acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with a target saturation of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 88 to 92 percent

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A controlled target of 88 to 92 percent gives adequate oxygen without suppressing the respiratory drive

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 94 to 98 percent: A target of 94 to 98 percent applies to most other acutely ill patients

C — 100 percent: A saturation of 100 percent risks carbon dioxide retention in these patients

D — 70 to 80 percent: A target of 70 to 80 percent is dangerously low

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Pearl: A rising drowsiness with a normal saturation suggests carbon dioxide retention, and a blood gas must be checked

question: A 64-year-old man is drowsy six hours after abdominal surgery and has a pulse of 118 per minute and a blood pressure of 96/60 mm Hg with a urine output of 15 mL in the last hour. The nurse should first:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. check the surgical site and dressing for bleeding, record the observations and inform the surgeon without delay

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Falling blood pressure with tachycardia, drowsiness and poor urine output suggests concealed bleeding or hypovolaemia, which must be reported immediately

🔍 Key Clues: 64-year-old | 118 per minute | 60 mm

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — wait for the next routine round: Waiting allows shock to progress unnoticed

C — increase the intravenous fluid rate on her own decision: Fluid rates are changed only on medical instruction, though a rapid review is requested

D — give a sedative so that he can rest: Sedation masks the signs of deterioration and is unsafe

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Pearl: Look at the dressing, the drain and the abdomen together, because internal bleeding may show no external sign
option_1: check the surgical site and dressing for bleeding, record the observations and inform the surgeon without delay
option_3: increase the intravenous fluid rate on her own decision
option_4: give a sedative so that he can rest

question: A patient with prolonged vomiting has a blood pH of 7.50 and a raised plasma bicarbonate. This picture indicates:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. metabolic alkalosis

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Loss of gastric acid in vomiting leaves an excess of bicarbonate, giving a high pH with a raised bicarbonate

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — metabolic acidosis: Metabolic acidosis has a low pH with a low bicarbonate

B — respiratory acidosis: Respiratory acidosis shows a high carbon dioxide with a low pH

C — respiratory alkalosis: Respiratory alkalosis follows overbreathing and shows a low carbon dioxide

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Pearl: Such a patient needs fluid and potassium replacement, because hypokalaemia worsens the alkalosis

question: Ten minutes after the start of a blood transfusion the patient develops fever, chills and flank pain. The nurse should first:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. stop the transfusion, keep the line open with saline and inform the doctor at once

🧠 Clinical Rationale: These are features of an acute haemolytic reaction, and the transfusion must be stopped immediately while the vein is kept open with saline

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give paracetamol and continue: Antipyretics mask the signs without treating the cause

C — slow the transfusion and continue to observe: Slowing the transfusion allows further incompatible blood to be given

D — add another unit of blood to dilute the reaction: Adding more blood worsens the reaction

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Pearl: Save the bag and the giving set and return them to the blood bank with fresh blood and urine samples, as the reaction must be investigated
option_2: stop the transfusion, keep the line open with saline and inform the doctor at once
option_3: slow the transfusion and continue to observe
option_4: add another unit of blood to dilute the reaction

question: Primary postpartum haemorrhage is defined as blood loss of more than:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 500 millilitres within 24 hours of vaginal delivery

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Loss of more than 500 millilitres after a vaginal birth, or more than 1000 millilitres after caesarean birth, within 24 hours is primary postpartum haemorrhage

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 100 millilitres at delivery: A loss of 100 millilitres is within normal limits

B — 200 millilitres within 6 weeks: This figure and time frame do not match the definition

D — 1000 millilitres within 7 days: Bleeding between 24 hours and six weeks after delivery is secondary postpartum haemorrhage, and the 1000 millilitre figure applies to caesarean birth

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

💎 PNC Pearl: Blood loss is often underestimated, so weighing the soaked pads gives a more reliable estimate
option_3: 500 millilitres within 24 hours of vaginal delivery

question: In active management of the third stage of labour, the uterotonic drug of choice is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. intramuscular oxytocin ten international units

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Ten international units of oxytocin given intramuscularly immediately after delivery of the baby makes the uterus contract and reduces blood loss

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — intravenous calcium gluconate: Calcium gluconate is used for magnesium toxicity and not for the third stage

C — oral iron: Iron is given for anaemia and has no effect on uterine contraction

D — intramuscular diazepam: Diazepam is a sedative and would not contract the uterus

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

💎 PNC Pearl: Oxytocin must be stored in a refrigerator because it loses potency when kept warm

question: Which finding in a woman at 34 weeks of pregnancy is most suggestive of severe pre-eclampsia?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. a blood pressure of 166/112 mm Hg with headache and blurred vision

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A blood pressure of 160/110 mm Hg or above with cerebral symptoms such as headache and visual disturbance indicates severe pre-eclampsia

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — mild ankle oedema in the evening: Mild evening ankle oedema is common in normal pregnancy

B — a blood pressure of 118/74 mm Hg: This reading is within the normal range

D — a single reading of 136/86 mm Hg: A single mildly raised reading is not diagnostic and should be repeated

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

💎 PNC Pearl: The definitive treatment for severe pre-eclampsia is delivery of the baby and placenta, so the team is alerted at once
option_3: a blood pressure of 166/112 mm Hg with headache and blurred vision

question: Bleaching powder is used in a village well mainly to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. disinfect the water by killing disease producing organisms

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Bleaching powder releases chlorine, which destroys bacteria and other organisms that cause water borne disease

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — remove the hardness of water: Hardness is due to dissolved salts of calcium and magnesium and is not removed by chlorination

B — increase the mineral content of the water: Chlorination does not add minerals to the water

D — improve the taste of the water: Chlorination may actually alter the taste, and taste is not the purpose

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

option_2: increase the mineral content of the water

question: A community health nurse finds three children in one lane with acute watery diarrhoea within a week. Which action is most appropriate?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. investigate the common water source and food handling, treat the affected children with oral rehydration and give health education to the families

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Clustering of cases points to a common source, so the nurse treats the cases and at the same time looks for and corrects the source

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — advise the families to move to another locality: Advising families to move is neither practical nor part of outbreak control

D — wait for more cases to appear before taking any action: Waiting allows an outbreak to spread

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

option_1: investigate the common water source and food handling, treat the affected children with oral rehydration and give health education to the families
option_2: advise the families to move to another locality
option_3: treat only the children who come to the clinic

question: Immunisation of children against measles is an example of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. primary prevention

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Primary prevention acts before disease occurs, and immunisation prevents the disease from developing at all

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — secondary prevention: Secondary prevention is early detection and prompt treatment of disease that has already begun

B — tertiary prevention: Tertiary prevention limits disability in established disease

D — rehabilitation: Rehabilitation is part of tertiary prevention and follows established disability

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

question: Which finding best shows that a breastfed newborn is receiving enough milk?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. six or more wet nappies a day, regular stools and steady weight gain after the initial loss

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Adequate intake is shown by a good urinary output, regular stools and weight gain after the physiological loss in the first week

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the baby passes urine twice a day: Two wet nappies a day is far below the expected number and suggests poor intake

option_3: the baby sleeps all day without waking for feeds

question: A 14-month-old child has a weight for height far below the expected value, visible severe wasting and pitting oedema of both feet. The priority in the first week of management is to:

question: Which combination of signs in a child with diarrhoea indicates severe dehydration?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. sunken eyes, a skin pinch that returns very slowly and lethargy or unconsciousness

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Two or more of sunken eyes, slow skin pinch and lethargy or unconsciousness classify the child as severely dehydrated under the integrated management approach

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a child who is thirsty with slightly sunken eyes: Thirst with slightly sunken eyes indicates some dehydration, which is treated with oral rehydration in the clinic

B — a playful child with moist mucous membranes: A playful child with moist membranes has no dehydration

D — a child who is alert with a dry mouth but normal skin turgor: A dry mouth with normal skin turgor usually means no dehydration

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: Severe dehydration needs an intravenous plan, whereas some dehydration is corrected with oral rehydration solution given over four hours

question: The specific antidote for paracetamol poisoning is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. N-acetylcysteine

🧠 Clinical Rationale: N-acetylcysteine replenishes glutathione and inactivates the toxic metabolite that damages the liver

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — atropine: Atropine is used for poisoning by organophosphates and for symptomatic bradycardia

B — deferoxamine: Deferoxamine is the chelating agent for iron poisoning

D — desferrioxamine and penicillin together: Combining these drugs does not treat paracetamol poisoning

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The antidote is most effective when given within eight to ten hours of ingestion, so the history of the time of ingestion is recorded carefully

question: A 34-year-old woman develops generalised itching, swollen eyelids and difficulty in breathing fifteen minutes after an injection of an antibiotic. The nurse should first:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. stop the drug, call for help, maintain the airway and give the prescribed adrenaline intramuscularly

🧠 Clinical Rationale: This is anaphylaxis, and stopping the drug while giving intramuscular adrenaline and supporting the airway is life saving

🔍 Key Clues: 34-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — give the next scheduled dose and observe: Continuing the drug will worsen the reaction

C — apply a cold compress to the eyes: A cold compress does nothing for a systemic reaction with breathing difficulty

D — record the reaction and inform the doctor at the next round: Delaying the report in a life threatening reaction is dangerous

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Intramuscular adrenaline into the outer thigh is the first drug in anaphylaxis and must be immediately available wherever injections are given
option_1: stop the drug, call for help, maintain the airway and give the prescribed adrenaline intramuscularly
option_2: give the next scheduled dose and observe

question: The part of the brain chiefly responsible for maintaining balance and coordinating voluntary movement is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. cerebellum

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The cerebellum coordinates posture, balance and smooth voluntary movement

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — hypothalamus: The hypothalamus controls temperature, hunger, thirst and autonomic functions

C — corpus callosum: The corpus callosum connects the two cerebral hemispheres

D — medulla oblongata: The medulla oblongata contains the vital centres for breathing and circulation

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: Cerebellar signs such as ataxia and an unsteady gait are tested in every neurological assessment

question: A 40-year-old man with a fracture of the shaft of the humerus is unable to extend his wrist and has numbness over the back of the hand. The nerve most likely injured is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. radial nerve

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The radial nerve runs in the spiral groove of the humerus, and its injury produces wrist drop with numbness over the dorsum of the hand

🔍 Key Clues: 40-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — median nerve: Median nerve injury affects thumb opposition and causes carpal tunnel symptoms

C — sciatic nerve: Sciatic nerve injury affects the leg and foot

D — ulnar nerve: Ulnar nerve injury produces claw hand and numbness of the little finger

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: Wrist drop after a humeral fracture is documented before and after plaster application, as the nerve may be compressed by the cast

question: The organism most commonly responsible for an uncomplicated urinary tract infection is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Escherichia coli

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Escherichia coli from the bowel is by far the commonest cause of uncomplicated urinary tract infection

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Staphylococcus aureus: Staphylococcus aureus more often causes skin, bone and bloodstream infection

B — Clostridium tetani: Clostridium tetani causes tetanus and has no role in urinary infection

C — Candida albicans: Candida affects the urinary tract mainly in catheterised or immunocompromised patients

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: A midstream specimen is collected before the first antibiotic dose so that the culture gives a true result

question: The cell that arrives first at the site of acute inflammation and engulfs bacteria is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. neutrophil

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Neutrophils migrate first to the site of acute inflammation and are the main phagocytic cells there

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — eosinophil: Eosinophils increase in allergic and parasitic conditions

B — plasma cell: Plasma cells appear later and produce antibodies

D — fibroblast: Fibroblasts lay down collagen during healing and are not phagocytes

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: A rising neutrophil count with fever supports a bacterial infection and is one of the reasons for a repeat blood count

question: The feature that distinguishes kwashiorkor from marasmus is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. pitting oedema with a relatively preserved subcutaneous fat layer

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Kwashiorkor is marked by oedema, poor hair and skin changes with some preserved subcutaneous fat, while in marasmus the child is grossly wasted

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a normal serum albumin level: The serum albumin is low in kwashiorkor because protein intake is deficient

B — severe wasting of muscles and loss of subcutaneous fat: Severe wasting is the hallmark of marasmus

C — a voracious appetite: Appetite is usually poor in kwashiorkor and relatively preserved in marasmus

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: Oedema hides weight loss, so weight is interpreted with the mid upper arm circumference and the clinical signs
option_2: severe wasting of muscles and loss of subcutaneous fat
option_4: pitting oedema with a relatively preserved subcutaneous fat layer

question: Which is the first step of the management process in a nursing unit?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. planning the objectives and activities of the unit

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Planning comes first and sets the objectives, priorities and methods on which the other steps depend

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — evaluating the performance of the staff: Evaluation is the final step and closes the loop

💎 PNC Pearl: An annual plan for the unit gives the basis on which staffing, equipment and training needs are justified to the administration
option_4: planning the objectives and activities of the unit

question: Choosing the patients who are most easily available to a nurse conducting a study is an example of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. convenience sampling

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Convenience sampling takes the subjects who are easiest to reach, and it is a non-probability method

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — systematic random sampling: Systematic sampling selects every nth person from a list

C — simple random sampling: Simple random sampling gives every member of the population an equal chance of selection

D — stratified random sampling: Stratified sampling divides the population into groups and samples each group

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: Convenience samples are prone to bias, so the reader must judge whether the findings can be applied to their own patients

question: Indian Standard Time is calculated from which longitude?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 82 degrees 30 minutes East

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Indian Standard Time is based on the longitude of 82 degrees 30 minutes East, which passes near Mirzapur

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 90 degrees East: 90 degrees East passes through Bangladesh and north eastern India

B — 68 degrees East: 68 degrees East marks the westernmost limit of the country

D — 75 degrees East: 75 degrees East passes near Ahmedabad and is far west of the standard meridian

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: A single time zone keeps drug rounds, duty changeover and referral timings uniform across the country

question: Kanchenjunga, the highest mountain peak in India, is situated in:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Sikkim

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Kanchenjunga stands on the border of Sikkim and Nepal and is the highest peak in India

❌ Why Not Other Options?

question: The headquarters of the International Labour Organization is situated in:
solution:

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The International Labour Organization has its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland

❌ Why Not Other Options?

question: The Right to Education Act came into force in the year:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 2010

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act came into force on the first of April, 2010

❌ Why Not Other Options?

question: National Nutrition Week is observed in India from:
solution:

question: World Mental Health Day is observed every year on:
solution:

question: Which of the following is the national aquatic animal of India?
solution:

❌ Why Not Other Options?

question: The first woman to become the President of the United Nations General Assembly was:
solution:
